memos.risk:
Risk officer call: refuse a buy at any size.

The brief is missing critical data: name and symbol are null, metadata host is null, curve bundle and completer shares are null, and the class is UNRESOLVED. We cannot tell whether this is operator-backed, which is the only category that has been roughly break-even.

The coin is also down 47% from its 30-minute high, with net flow of +1.57 SOL in the last 15 minutes against 200 SOL of gross buying, so momentum is fading. A launch bot was present, and sells roughly matched buys in the first two minutes.

Pool depth of about 90 SOL means a $20 ticket would already cost a meaningful share of the round-trip 1.4-5.1% range, and exits in a falling market would be worse.

If the desk ever revisits this coin, the minimum would be resolved class, metadata, and curve concentration data showing operator backing. Even then, the sizing would be the $5 floor with a 20% stop and a 15-minute hold.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying is weak. The best evidence is that the coin is alive: 340 buyers and 287 sellers in the last 15 minutes, $48k volume, and 139 buyers in the first two minutes after graduation with a top-5 buyer share of only 26%, which argues against a single operator. The 30-minute return of +28.6% shows it did run.

But the signals that matter for the next 30-60 minutes point the wrong way. Price is 47% off its 30-minute high and still falling (-6.1% over 15 minutes). Net flow over the last 15 minutes is essentially flat (+1.57 SOL on 200 SOL of buying), meaning sellers absorbed almost every dollar of new demand. The sell-to-buy ratio in the launch window was 1.09, so early buyers were already exiting. The curve data (bundle share, completer share, graduation delay) is entirely unresolved, so we cannot rule out a factory or dumped-supply pattern. The launch bot is present, and the name and symbol are null, so there is no visible identity to anchor demand.

Against a round trip cost of 1.4-5.1%, the drawdown and flat flow do not show demand that will persist. My recommendation is to skip this coin.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss here is a fade of the spike that already happened. The coin is 30.5 minutes old, up 28.6% at its 30-minute mark, but 47.2% below its 30-minute high, so the move is already reversing. In the last 15 minutes, 287 sellers against 340 buyers pushed net flow to just +1.57 SOL on roughly 200 SOL of gross volume, with a -6.1% return. That's churn, not conviction. Post-graduation, sell-to-buy was 1.09 with a launch bot present, and the curve data is unresolved (no bundle or top-3 share), so insider distribution can't be ruled out. The pool is only 90 SOL deep, so a $20 round trip at 1.4-5.1% cost needs a clean 5%+ move that this chart isn't showing. Skip.
